the most popular volatility measures have a comparable performance in terms of forecasting volatility, that the best measure is not always the same for each model, that the best volatility model is not always the best for every volatility measure and that different loss functions can lead to different results.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the context of volatility prediction, the choice of a specific model and loss function should be made before the selection of an appropriate measure.
there is no best volatility measure for all volatility models and loss functions.
the best measure for the prediction of volatility is the one which is used in the model which is used for the loss function which is used for forecasting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
volatility prediction is a very complex task and should be considered with care.
the HAR model is the best choice for forecasting daily volatility, whereas the MIDAS approach is the best for forecasting weekly and monthly volatility.
the best measure is model-dependent and the best model is measure-dependent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the appropriate volatility measure and model is a crucial issue for volatility forecasting and should not be neglected in empirical studies.
the choice of a volatility measure should be made carefully and should take the volatility model and loss function into consideration.
the HAR and MIDAS models tend to perform better than a standard GARCH(1,1) model for the considered data set, whereas the empirical similarity approach tends to perform worse.
